scope: SQLite official FTS3/FTS4 and FTS5 documentation; internal details vary with source version and build options

claims.claim: FTS3 has been available since SQLite 3.5.0 (2007-09-04); the FTS4 enhancements were added in 3.7.4 (2010-12-07)
claims.notes: Corrects the earlier page dates (3.6.0/2009 and 3.7.4/2011)

claims.claim: An FTS3/FTS4 index is a set of b-tree segments; each segment entry has a term key and a doclist of (docid, term-offset list) pairs
The unicode61 tokenizer is available beginning with SQLite 3.7.13 (2012-06-11); simple, porter and icu are the other bundled tokenizers
FTS3/FTS4 expose special commands optimize, rebuild, integrity-check, merge=X,Y and automerge=N; merge Y must be between 2 and 16 with a recommended value of 8
claims.locator: 7. Special Commands For FTS3 and FTS4

claims.claim: FTS5 is a separate module (added in 3.9.0) with its own index format, a built-in rank column and its own tokenizer options; it does not share the fts3.c implementation
claims.notes: Pointer for readers; not independently re-read this session, treat exact API surface as version-scoped

claims.claim: A MATCH query should drive the full-text lookup directly; wrapping it in rowid IN (SELECT ...) can bypass the FTS index and force per-row checks
claims.notes: Teaching guidance; actual plan depends on the query and SQLite version
